title: Getting started
summary: The start screen, the interface tour and the Cedar House sample
steps: A free, native Mac app for drafting and building design
The Cedar House: the house this tutorial series builds step by step
Tools grouped in tabs; every button runs a command you could also type
The 2D plan of the current level: scroll to zoom, drag to pan
Just start typing: commands, options and coordinates
Properties, Layers, Levels, project Browser, Materials and more
Snaps, grid, ortho and polar tracking toggles, cursor coordinates
Switch the workspace with these buttons or ⌥⌘1–4
Tutorial 02 shows how to drive the app by typing

title: The command line
summary: Commands, aliases, coordinates, options, repeat and undo
steps: Commands go straight to the command line; Enter or Space confirms
L is LINE, C is CIRCLE, REC is RECTANG, PL is PLINE…
Type the capital letters of an option: D for Diameter
An empty Enter starts CIRCLE again
U undoes the last command, REDO brings it back
↑ and ↓ recall earlier lines; F2 shows the whole history
Tutorial 03 covers snaps, ortho, trim, offset and fillet

title: Drawing basics
summary: Lines, polylines, rectangles, circles, snaps, ortho, trim, offset and fillet
steps: Rectangles, circles and polylines with arc segments
OSNAP locks the cursor to endpoints, midpoints and centres
F8 keeps lines horizontal or vertical; type a length to go that far
FILLET rounds the corner between two lines
TRIM cuts objects back to the edges they cross
OFFSET makes parallel copies at a distance

title: Levels and walls
summary: Levels, walls with thickness, height and justification, wall types and joins
steps: Every building element belongs to a level (storey)
WALL draws a chain of joined walls; Thickness and Height are options
A taller chain: 7.2 m, joined to the wing
3.3 m walls around the entrance and the kitchen
Walls are drawn by their centre line, or their left or right face
The Type option lists and edits layered wall types
A thin 120 mm partition T-joins the walls automatically

title: Doors and windows
summary: Placing windows and doors in walls, types, sizes, openings and flipping
steps: WINDOW places a window where you pick a wall
Width, Height and Sill: a tall window high in the wall
A 5.3 m glazing strip and a high window
The Type option lists the door types of the project
A 1100 × 2700 pivot door, full-height glazing and a sidelight
OPENINGFLIP turns a door to open the other way
OPENING cuts an empty doorway in the partition
Openings cut through their walls and move with them

title: Floors, roofs and stairs
summary: Slabs, flat and shed roofs with overhangs, a stair between levels and the canopy
steps: SLAB from points: 250 mm oak floors
Offset raises a slab above its level: 180 mm
Kind, Overhang and Base (eave height) are options
A 4° mono-pitch plate with a deep 1.3 m overhang on the tower
A 450 mm slab at 3.75 m over the whole entry wing
STAIR runs to the Upper Floor level; the risers are computed
Set the level current and draw its slab

title: Rooms and annotation
summary: Rooms with areas, dimensions, text, tags and hatches
steps: ROOM: click inside the walls; the area is computed
DIMLINEAR: two points, then where the dimension line goes
TEXT: position, height, rotation, then the words
TAGALL labels every door, window and room with live values
Draw a boundary and fill it with a pattern
SCHEDULE lists the rooms with their areas and volumes

title: 3D and materials
summary: The 3D view, orbiting, visual styles, materials and textures, and the section box
steps: The model is always live: every plan edit shows in 3D
Drag to orbit, scroll to zoom, the view cube jumps to standard views
VSCURRENT: Realistic, Shaded, Hidden line, Conceptual, X-ray, Sketchy
Colour, roughness, metalness, transparency and textures
Pick in the plan, then CHPROP Material
Cut the model live to look inside

title: Rendering
summary: Sun position, render presets, saved cameras and a final render to an image
steps: CAMERA restores the views saved with the project
SUNSTUDY: date and time sliders; the shadows follow the solar position
Orbit to a view you like and SAVECAMERA it
RENDER opens the render window: presets from Draft to Print 4K
Sky, sun, exposure, ambient occlusion and soft shadows
RENDERTOFILE: size, pass, style and the image path
Tutorial 10 lays out drawings on paper

title: Sheets and PDF
summary: Sheets, viewports at a scale, the title block and plotting to PDF
steps: LAYOUT New adds a paper sheet (A3 landscape by default)
MVIEW: corners in paper millimetres, a scale and a view
Elevations, sections and 3D views are generated from the model
Sheet title, number, scale and date, plus project information
PLOT writes the current sheet to a vector PDF at true scale
PUBLISH writes every sheet into one multi-page PDF
Tutorial 11 exchanges the model with other software

title: Import and export
summary: DXF, IFC, OBJ and GLB export, schedules to CSV and IFC import
steps: EXPORT DXF: the plan for AutoCAD and other CAD software
EXPORT IFC: walls, slabs, doors, windows and spaces for BIM software
OBJ and GLB for 3D software, game engines and the web
SCHEDULE builds tables of doors, windows, rooms and walls
EXPORT CSV writes the schedules for spreadsheets
IFCIMPORT reads IFC into native, editable elements
Also: DWG, Rhino, SketchUp, STEP, PDF…
File ▸ Import and IMPORTFILE accept many more formats

title: Scripting and AI
summary: The JavaScript console, the archi API, the agent server and archi-cli --mcp for Claude
steps: SCRIPTCONSOLE (⌥⌘J): JavaScript with an archi object
Commands, documents and building elements from code
AI agents drive the open drawing through a local JSON-RPC server
archi-cli --mcp is a Model Context Protocol server for Claude
